Rylee Wirt Datasheet as part of Garden Buddy for Team 201

Submission: October 26, 2025

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This data sheet will give a detailed overview of my subsystem design for the Irri-gators Team 201 project. It will explain the function, power requirements, and the integration of my design with my fellow teammates. It will also help others understand how the circuit operates and where to locate specific details of componenets.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
Team 201: The Irri-gators is developing an irrigation control system that is designed to be able to monitor your plants hydration level and then water the plants accordingly. To do this we are using sensors, actuators, and microcontroller-based logic. My portion of this project is designing the speaker subsystem which provides audio-based feedback to show the systems status, different alerts, and possible errors. The subsystem uses a Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Board to process input signals that are recieved through an 8-pin connector. From there the signals are amplified by an op amp and then output through a speaker. The power for this system is supplied by a 5 Volt 1.5 Amp voltage regulator to maintain consistent operation.

This datasheet is just one part of our larger report. For more details about the rest of the system please refer to the full team report at this link: https://asu-egr304-2025-f-201.github.io

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
My part of working with team 201 is designing, testing, and documenting our speaker subsystem. My design provides a reliable way to generate audio-based signals that alert the user to our designs activity or different errors that the system might be experiencing. During this I collaborated with my teammates to define signal interfaces and power distribution to maintain compatibility across our different subsystems.

This datasheet allows readers to navigate the various technical aspects of my contribution. To review the materials used in constructing this subsystem, refer to the "BOM" (Bill of Materials) section. For schematics, power analysis, or performance testing results, see the relevant sections within this document. Together, these provide a detailed analysis and understanding of how the speaker system supports Team 201's project Garden Buddy.

To review the details listed of the material used to construct the subsection, you can review it in the "BOM" section of the datasheet.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This block diagram shows my design for a speaker system for Team 201: The Irri-gators water system product. The Microchip pic18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Board processes input from the 8-pin connector, which then sends a signal to the op amp for amplification, then to the speaker for sound generation. There's a 5 volt 1.5 amp voltage regulator to provide a consistent and stable power source for the components. Also included is a button and LED for testing purposes. Overall, this diagram shows how the system works, how it's tested, and how it's designed to integrate into the rest of my teams systems.

docs.title: 1. Light Sensor (Ambient Light Detection)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet TEMT6000 (already in kit) - Already available in kit - Small and easy to interface with PIC - Meets project spec - Limited spectral sensitivity - Not waterproof $0.75 Vishay TEMT6000 Datasheet TSL2561 Digital Light Sensor - I2C digital output - High dynamic range - Built-in lux calculation - Needs I2C support on PIC - Slightly larger footprint $3.95 TSL2561 Datasheet BH1750 Ambient Light Sensor - Digital I2C interface - High accuracy - Compact - Requires extra library for PIC - Needs external pull-ups $2.50 BH1750 Datasheet

Choice: TEMT6000 Rationale: Already in kit, easy to integrate with PIC ADC, meets project light detection requirement without additional setup.

docs.title: 2. Rail-to-Rail Op-Amp (Signal Conditioning)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet MCP6004-I/P (already in kit) - Already available - Rail-to-rail I/O - Compatible with 5 V PIC supply - Limited bandwidth - Low current drive $0.44 MCP6004 Datasheet LM358 Dual Op-Amp - Low cost - Widely available - Can handle multiple signals - Not rail-to-rail - Slightly higher offset voltage $0.25 LM358 Datasheet TLV2372 Rail-to-Rail Op-Amp - Rail-to-rail input/output - Low noise - Small footprint - Slightly more expensive - Not in kit $0.85 TLV2372 Datasheet

Choice: MCP6004-I/P Rationale: Already in kit, rail-to-rail, sufficient for amplifying sensor signals. Minimizes cost and time.

docs.title: 3. Push Buttons (User Input)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet Tactile Push Button (already in kit) - Already available - Easy to wire - Inexpensive - Small size - Limited lifespan $0.10 Tactile Switch Datasheet Omron B3F-4050 - Longer lifespan - Tactile feedback - Compact - Slightly larger - More expensive $0.50 Omron B3F-4050 Datasheet Alps SKQGAAE010 - Smooth tactile feel - High durability - Not in kit - Requires careful PCB layout $0.75 Alps SKQGAAE010 Datasheet

Choice: Kit Push Button Rationale: Already available, meets mechanical and electrical requirements, minimal effort needed.

docs.title: 4. Red LED (Visual Alert)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet 5 mm Red LED (already in kit) - Already available - Easy to interface - Compact - Low brightness in sunlight - Requires series resistor $0.05 Vishay 5mm Red LED Datasheet Kingbright WP7113ID - High brightness - Wide viewing angle - Not in kit - Slightly higher cost $0.20 WP7113 Datasheet Cree CLM2F-RRD-CT - Extremely bright - Long life - Not in kit - Expensive $1.50 CLM2F Datasheet

Choice: Kit LED Rationale: Already available, sufficient brightness indoors, easy to integrate.

docs.title: 5. Speaker (Audio Alert)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet 8 Ω Mylar Mini Speaker (already in kit) - Already available - Compact - Works with small signal amplifiers - Limited sound output - Not high-fidelity $0.85 CE-2808B36 Datasheet Adafruit Mini Speaker 8 Ω 0.5 W - Small and easy to wire - Moderate volume - Not in kit - Slightly higher cost $2.95 Adafruit Mini Speaker Datasheet CUI CDM-10008 - Compact - Decent volume - Not in kit - Needs amplifier $1.25 CDM-10008 Datasheet

Choice: Kit Mini Speaker Rationale: Already in kit, small size, functional, and meets project audio alert needs.

docs.title: 6. Voltage Regulator (5 V Supply)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet LM7805 Linear Regulator (already in kit) - Already available - Simple to use - Stable 5 V output - Inefficient at high currents - Heat dissipation for >1 A $0.43 LM7805 Datasheet LM2940 Low Dropout 5 V Regulator - Low dropout - Better efficiency than 7805 - Not in kit - Needs input capacitor $1.00 LM2940 Datasheet Switching Buck Converter 5 V Module - High efficiency - Can provide more current - Needs careful layout - EMI possible $3.50 16060 Datasheet

Choice: LM7805 Rationale: Already in kit, provides reliable 5 V output for the system, simple implementation, and requires no additional components beyond standard input/output capacitors.

docs.title: 7. Potentiometer (Adjustable Threshold)
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Cost Datasheet 10 kΩ Trim Pot (already in kit) - Already available - Adjustable light threshold - Easy to interface - Small size - Limited adjustment range $0.15 65040 Datasheet Bourns 3296W Multi-Turn Pot - High precision - Multi-turn adjustment - Not in kit - Slightly larger $1.00 3296W Datasheet Alps RK09 Potentiometer - Smooth adjustment - Compact - Not in kit - Higher cost $1.25 RK09 Datasheet

Choice: Kit 10 kΩ Trim Pot Rationale: Already available, meets project threshold adjustment needs, minimal assembly time.
